slides.9.title: Key Takeaways
slides.9.points.0: Wine Advocate (Robert Parker 100-point scale) has the strongest influence on Barolo/Brunello prices — a score of 98–100 can drive a 200–400% price surge
slides.9.points.1: Three vintage tiers: legendary (98–100 pts), excellent (93–97 pts), challenging (85–92 pts)
slides.9.points.2: Vintage climate science: September–October pre-harvest autumn rain and diurnal temperature range are the most critical factors for Nebbiolo quality
slides.9.points.4: En Primeur: enter 1–2 years post-harvest; legendary vintage early-bird pricing is 20–40% below release — but requires a 4–5 year wait for delivery
slides.9.points.5: Vertical collections (same estate, multiple vintages) are highly coveted at auction; horizontal (same vintage, multiple estates) balances learning with liquidity
slides.9.points.6: Best buying moment: 3 months before score release or during market pessimism; best selling: 6–12 months after high scores or at the start of the drinking window
slides.9.points.7: Long-term holding of Monfortino and Biondi-Santi yields ~8–15% annualised returns; En Primeur arbitrage targets 50–100% over 3–5 years
slides.9.points.8: Keeping the OWC (Original Wooden Case) can increase auction estimates by 15–25%; Provenance documentation is a mandatory requirement for auction submission

quiz.0.question: Which rating system has the greatest influence on Italian fine wine investment?
quiz.0.explanation: Wine Advocate's 100-point scale has the strongest influence on Italian fine wine market prices, especially for Barolo and Brunello — a score of 98–100 can cause prices to surge 200–400%.
quiz.1.question: How do wine critics classify the Piemonte 2016 vintage?
quiz.1.explanation: 2016 is one of the greatest Piemonte vintages in decades — Wine Advocate awarded 100 points. The growing season was perfect, Nebbiolo achieved ideal ripeness-acidity balance, and ageing potential exceeds 50 years.
quiz.2.question: What is the definition of a Vertical Collection?
quiz.2.options.0: Storing wine bottles in an upright position
quiz.2.options.1: A series collection of the same estate across multiple consecutive vintages
quiz.2.options.2: Comparing the same vintage across multiple different estates
quiz.2.options.3: A collection arranged by alcohol level
quiz.2.explanation: A Vertical Collection means collecting the same estate across multiple consecutive vintages (e.g. Giacomo Conterno Monfortino 1990–2016), allowing you to observe how the same terroir expresses itself under different climate conditions. Complete vertical series are highly sought at auction.
quiz.3.question: What is the ideal storage temperature for Italian fine wine?
quiz.3.explanation: The ideal storage temperature for fine wine is 12–14°C — never above 18°C, never below 7°C. Temperature fluctuation is more damaging than a consistently slightly elevated temperature; professional temperature-controlled storage is essential.
quiz.4.question: Which Tuscany vintage is rated the greatest for Brunello in nearly 30 years?
quiz.4.explanation: 2015 is one of Tuscany's greatest vintages in nearly 30 years — Brunello di Montalcino combines power and elegance, Wine Advocate awarded 100 points, and ageing potential reaches 40–50 years.
quiz.5.question: What is the greatest investment risk of En Primeur (futures)?
quiz.5.options.0: En Primeur can only be purchased inside Italy
quiz.5.options.1: Capital is locked for a long period (Brunello requires 4–5 years), and quality is uncertain at the time of purchase
quiz.5.options.2: En Primeur cannot be resold through auction houses
quiz.5.options.3: En Primeur is more expensive than the wine after official release
quiz.5.explanation: The main risk of En Primeur is capital lock-up: Brunello requires 5 years of legal ageing, so futures buyers must wait 4–5 years before receiving the wine and cannot cancel mid-way. Quality must be judged before scores are released.
